prespecification_note: Written and checksum-pinned before the model was evaluated at the CAN-1004 sampling times. Not blinded: the CAN-1004 Table 7 values were read before writing this plan, and from 3.0f it was known that the model's single-dose AUC to infinity at 1.3 mg/m2 is about 141 ng.h/mL and that its emulated day 11 AUC was consistent with Ogawa 2008. No emulated value for the CAN-1004 schedule had been computed.
not_this: Not validation or qualification of the PK model; no acceptance limits are introduced.
Not a comparison of individual concentrations; only Table 7 means and SDs are available.
Not a re-fit: no parameter is estimated or tuned.
Not a dosing or exposure prediction for any patient.
question: Does the 3.0f finding (constant-clearance model over-predicts first-dose exposure and under-predicts the rise to day 11) hold in a second, non-Japanese study with 72 h sampling (CAN-1004, IV arm)?

data.model: intelligence_store/bortezomib_pk.py (exact three-compartment solution; Lignet 2022 Table 1 per-m2 parameters), unchanged from 3.0f

simulation.regimen: IV bolus 1.3 mg/m2 at t = 0, 72, 168 and 240 h; no drug before t = 0.
simulation.body_size: Not needed: dose and model parameters are per m2, so concentrations do not depend on BSA. Clearance in L/h is not compared because patient BSA is not reported.
simulation.day1_profile: Model concentration at each CAN-1004 sampling time after t = 0; the 72 h sample is taken before the day 4 dose.
simulation.day11_profile: Model concentration at each sampling time after t = 240 h, including drug remaining from the doses on days 1, 4 and 8.

nca_emulation.method: Same function as 3.0f (bortezomib_pk_ogawa_check.nca): C0 by log-linear back-extrapolation from the first two samples (2 and 5 min); AUC to the last sample (72 h) by trapezoids from (0, C0); terminal slope over the last points; AUC to infinity adds C_last / slope.

secondary.name: auc_inf_day1, auc_inf_day11
secondary.why_secondary: depend on the terminal-phase method, which is not reported

descriptive: ratio of means AUClast day 11 / day 1 (observed 241 / 104 = 2.32); no interval, because per-patient ratios are not reported
the same model's 3.0f results against Ogawa 2008, for side-by-side reading

comparison.interval: 95% confidence interval of the observed mean: mean +/- t(0.975, 9) x SD / sqrt(10), t = 2.2622.
comparison.robustness: Each classified endpoint under all four NCA readings; robust if all four agree.

decision_rule.summary: The model is recorded as consistent with CAN-1004 only if both primary endpoints are consistent under the primary reading. The 3.0f day 1 finding is recorded as reproduced in a second study if AUClast day 1 is over-predicted; as not reproduced if consistent. The rise is assessed descriptively.
decision_rule.never: No parameter is re-estimated or tuned. The model is not changed by this check.

known_differences: Typical-value model compared with arithmetic means of skewed quantities (day 1 AUClast SD 99 on a mean of 104).
The sponsor's NCA settings are not reported; four readings bracket the usual choices.
Concomitant dexamethasone and other study conditions are not described in the review pages used.
